memory_candidates.content: When a markdown-consolidation inventory names a duplicated block that is EMBEDDED inside a larger complete, literal copy-paste example/skeleton (e.g. a full report-template or plan-template fenced code block, where the matched duplicate is only a 2-5 line sub-fragment of a 20+ line skeleton), do not collapse the sub-fragment alone -- doing so leaves the surrounding template structurally incomplete/inconsistent relative to its own heading list, which defeats the template's purpose (an agent must be able to copy the whole skeleton verbatim). Recognize this as a THIRD exclusion class alongside gate-required and deliberately-inlined content: 'embedded in a complete copy-paste template.' Record it as a Reasoned Exclusion with the anchor's own fenced-block location as evidence, not as a silent skip.

A doc-lint check that derives its 'files on disk' set from `git ls-files` (tracked files only) will not fire on a genuine gap until the affected files are actually tracked -- a prior phase's new data files (e.g. lint-registry capture files) can silently carry an undeclared-in-manifest gap for an arbitrary number of later commits/phases before anyone's gate run happens to re-trigger the check with those files already staged. When adding new files under any extension's scripts/ tree (even non-.sh data files like .txt/.tsv captures a registry-driven lint consumes), re-run the manifest-sync check/write tool (if one exists, e.g. sync-manifest-scripts.sh) immediately after `git add`-ing them, not just after writing them -- staging is the trigger, not authoring.
